item.text: The source supports keeping the workflow overview central and expanding input capture, execution, output handling, and evaluation in separate trees. I also found two qualifications to preserve: promotion follows links across the selected canvas even when promoting one diagram, and bulk deletion keeps reruns that were not selected.

229: export function validatePromptStages(workflow: EvalWorkflow, stages: Record<string, string>, references?: ReadonlySet<string>) {
230:   const issues: Record<string, TemplateIssue[]> = {};
231:   for (const stage of workflow.stages) issues[stage.id] = validateTemplate(stages[stage.id] ?? '', workflow.variables, references);
232:   for (const key of Object.keys(stages)) if (!workflow.stages.some(stage => stage.id === key))
233:     (issues[key] ??= []).push({ severity: 'error', message: `Unknown stage ${key}.` });
234:   return issues;
235: }
236: export const promptHasErrors = (issues: Record<string, TemplateIssue[]>) => Object.values(issues).some(list => list.some(issue => issue.severity === 'error'));
237: 
238: /** Execution only substitutes visible variables; it never adds or replaces instructions. */
239: export function composePrompt(workflow: EvalWorkflow, stageId: string, body: string, values: Record<string, string>, base?: PromptTemplateBase) {
240:   const stage = workflow.stages.find(item => item.id === stageId);
241:   if (!stage) throw Error(`Unknown stage ${stageId}`);
242:   return renderPromptSections(body, base ?? legacyPromptTemplateBase({ body }), text => renderTemplate(text, values));
243: }
